stem:
Urvashi's graph compares English and Hindi marks for Divya, Kabir, and Neel with adjacent bars, one common scale, and a legend.

One or more options may be correct. Which two claims correctly describe how the graph is built?

options.text: For each student, two adjacent bars share the category, use the same vertical scale, and the legend separates English from Hindi.
Bar heights on the common scale can be compared across English and Hindi for the same student.
The display is finished by naming it a double column graph, without comparing any bar heights.
Drawing the clustered bars is what creates the English and Hindi marks.

teacher.key_rationale: A clustered column graph places related bars side by side for each student, keeps one common scale, and uses a legend so heights can be compared. Naming the graph type alone substitutes a label. Saying the bars create the marks reverses the encoding.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source figure as a clustered double-column graph of English and Hindi marks for Divya, Kabir, and Neel.
